prompt: Write a C++ token-bucket rate limiter: rate_limiter.h and rate_limiter.cc, with a TokenBucket class supporting a blocking Acquire(n) and a non-blocking TryAcquire(n). Comments must be complete.

configs.with_skill_cc1: Skill loaded, prompt prefixed with 'CC1.' (concise tier, also the default)
configs.with_skill_cc2: Skill loaded, prompt prefixed with 'CC2.' (full-detail tier)

assertions: TokenBucket class comment in the .h says what the class is for and states its thread-safety guarantee explicitly
Every public method declaration in the .h has a contract comment: what it does, parameter meaning/units, return value semantics
Acquire documents its blocking semantics (and timeout behavior if a timeout is offered); TryAcquire documents True/False semantics and that nothing is consumed on failure
Units are documented for rates and durations (tokens per second, seconds)
Function comments are third-person declarative with proper punctuation
The .cc does not duplicate the .h contract comments; its comments explain implementation choices (e.g. why sleeping outside the lock / condition-variable usage)
No comments that restate the code; no Author: lines; // style used consistently
If any call site passes a bare literal argument, it uses the /*param_name=*/value comment form (vacuously true if no such call exists)
assertions_cc1: Every comment block is at most 3 sentences
No usage-example code blocks inside comments
